title: Per-layer comm/compute overlap profiling for mixed-precision shards
content:
Purpose:
This doc records an experiment plan and early results for measuring per-layer communication vs compute overlap when using mixed-precision weight shards (FP16/BF16) in tensor- and pipeline-parallel inference. Goal is to identify which layers and shard placements are dominating tail latency and to validate whether increased compute-to-comm overlap via async kernels or slice reordering yields measurable latency/throughput gains for our production-like request workloads.

Background / motivation:
- We routinely see tail latency inflations on 8x A100 nodes for medium-sequence chat workloads even when median latency looks fine.
- Hypothesis: Mixed-precision changes compute latency per-layer (different kernel selection) and can change the ratio of comm to compute for specific transformer blocks, which changes the effectiveness of our overlap strategies.
- Existing profiling artifacts are coarse (per-step aggregate, NCCL timeline slices) — need per-layer breakdowns (send/recv, kernel launch, cudaEvent gaps) and correlation with shard layout.

What we want to measure:
1) Per-layer breakdown of: compute kernel time (forward matmul, attention, kv cache ops), NCCL send/recv time, host staging / memcpy, and idle gaps where the GPU waits for data.
2) For different numeric formats (FP32 baseline, FP16, BF16) and quantization-friendly kernels (e.g., fused-ggml-like kernels), measure how comm/compute ratio shifts per layer.
3) For two parallelization strategies: (a) tensor-parallel weight-sharding (1D row or column), (b) pipeline-parallel micro-batching — measure overlap effectiveness.
4) Explore a small set of mitigations: prefetching KV segments, interleaving small layers to increase compute granularity, and asynchronous NCCL progress/polling tweaks.

Experiment matrix (initial):
- Hardware: 4x and 8x A100 (PCIe and NVLink topo variants where possible).
- Model: small-medium decoder-only (1.8B) and large decoder (13B) to observe scale effects.
- Precision: FP32, FP16, BF16.
- Shard modes: replicated, tensor-parallel-col (TP-col), tensor-parallel-row (TP-row), pipeline-2 (2 stages), pipeline-4 (4 stages).
- Workloads: single-request latency (seq_len 1024), bursty concurrent requests (QPS 50, 200), and mixed PLG-like burst (few 1-token then long continuations).
- Instrumentation profiles: CUDA events around kernels, CUPTI API for kernel durations, NCCL tracepoints for send/recv and enqueue times, host-side timestamps for memcpy and queueing delays.

Instrumentation and measurement details:
- Add per-layer annotated markers in runtime (layer id, op type). On entry/exit of each major op (attention, ff, layernorm, kv load), place cudaEvent record (start/end). Use CUPTI to capture kernel names and durations and map them to layer ids.
- NCCL: enable NCCL_TRACE_LEVEL=INFO to get op-level timings; instrument our NCCL wrappers to emit layer id and message size with event timestamps (enqueue, start-fence, end-fence).
- Host staging: measure pinned-host memcpy times and time spent waiting in host queues before DMA submission.
- OS/driver counters: collect NVPROF/CUPTI counters for memory throughput, PCIe bandwidth counters when available to see when links saturate.
- Correlate all timelines using monotonic clocks and wallclock offsets; we will normalize timings to per-token and per-layer metrics for easier comparison.

Key metrics to extract per experiment run:
- compute_ms_per_layer: median and p95
- comm_ms_per_layer: median and p95 (split by NCCL send/recv and host memcpy)
- idle_ms_per_layer: gaps where compute hasn't started but comm hasn't completed (shows bad overlap)
- comm_volume_bytes_per_layer and effective_bandwidth_GBps
- overlap_ratio = compute_time / (compute_time + comm_time + idle_time) — rough indicator of how much time is overlapped
- end-to-end tail latency (p99) and throughput (tokens/s)

Preliminary findings (pilot runs, 4x A100, 1.8B model):
- FP16 vs BF16: FP16 kernels are ~8-12% faster on average for matmuls on this kernel set, reducing per-layer compute time. However, for several attention-heavy layers (middle layers in transformer), compute speedup increased comm dominance: comm_ms_per_layer became a larger share, and overlap_ratio dropped for those layers by ~15%.
- TP-col vs TP-row: TP-col tends to have larger allreduce/transpose-like comm patterns that create bigger NCCL messages but fewer messages overall. TP-row had many smaller messages which increased NCCL latency and host staging overhead; p99 latency was ~9% worse for TP-row at medium QPS.
- Pipeline stages: pipeline-4 with microbatching improved throughput but increased idle gaps at stage boundaries when using FP16 because kernels finished earlier and had to wait for cross-stage transfers.

Observed micro-patterns of interest:
- Small-kernel churn: layers with small matmuls (<1MB payload) create many short NCCL ops; our current NCCL progress polling interval (20ms default in runtime loop) means many of these operations don't get timely progress, creating tiny idle gaps that add up to 6-12% of total p99 latency.
- KV prefetch mismatch: when using mixed precision, the size of KV segments changed slightly (data packing), and our prefetch window (fixed token lookahead) didn't match, causing late host memcpys observed as 1-3ms spikes on stage transitions.
- Asymmetric compute: earlier layers are heavier in compute, later layers heavier in comm after quantized kernels kick in — suggests we can rearrange shard orientation (e.g., put TP-col on layers with high comm tolerance).

Proposed mitigations to test next (implementation notes):
1) Reduce host polling intervals and enable NCCL async progress threads for short-message workloads, measure CPU overhead.
2) Adjust prefetch lookahead dynamically based on per-layer comm_volume_bytes and observed memcpy latency (simple heuristic: prefetch_size_ms = max( default, 2 * moving_avg_memcpy_ms ) ).
3) Layer grouping: schedule two small consecutive layers without interleaving NCCL flush to create bigger contiguous compute so overlap becomes more effective.
4) Message coalescing: aggregate multiple small NCCL messages when they target same ring/peer — requires runtime batching at tensor-shard granularity.
5) Hybrid shard policy: use a per-layer policy file that chooses TP-col/TP-row based on measured overlap_ratio and comm_volume.

Implementation risks and constraints:
- Async progress threads can increase CPU usage and may compete with host staging threads — need test for regression under heavy QPS.
- Coalescing increases complexity and could hurt memory footprint (temporarily buffer more data).
- Per-layer policies require safe fallback with versioned rollout; we must ensure correctness across model versions and checkpointing.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run full matrix on 8x NVLink box (requested via infra: ticket INFRA-GPU-371).
- [ ] Hook up automated pipeline to generate per-layer CSVs and a dashboard (Grafana) to visualize overlap_ratio heatmaps across layers and experiments. (Ava to proto.)
- [ ] Implement lightweight NCCL coalescer prototype in branch perf/overlap-coalesce and run microbenchmarks. (Ethan)
- [ ] Evaluate async-progress thread effect on CPU and p99 with QPS 200 bursty workload.
- [ ] Draft short runbook describing when to prefer TP-col vs TP-row based on observed metrics for customers running 4–16 GPU clusters.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is there a kernel level optimization we can apply to make compute slightly slower but more batch-friendly to improve overlap (counterintuitive but may help tail)?
- How aggressive should automatic per-layer reshuffling be vs. a conservative default?
- Are there hardware-specific knobs (NVLink pacing or driver-level reordering) we can surface via our config?

Appendix: quick commands used in pilot runs:
- Runtime flags: --enable-cupti=1 --layer-markers=1 --ncc l-progress=thread --prefetch-lookahead=4
- NCCL envs: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=22 NCCL_ALGO=RING
- Profiling: cupti_trace.py --pid <server_pid> --map-layers layers.map --out pilot1.cupti

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally an early, somewhat messy notes doc documenting findings and next experiments. Please add contradictory observations if you have runs that disagree (esp. on BF16 vs FP16 behavior).
- If you have strong opinions on message coalescing vs prefetch tuning, add notes inline or by PR on linked GitHub branch.
